equivalents.note: The Tibetan line has ri bong 'dzin pa'i chu, 'the water of the hare-holder', that is, the moon's water, where the Bengali has the poet take the moon and sprinkle water.
The rendering is plain, but the string དུ་བ also occurs across word boundaries (du followed by bshad, bya and so on), so it cannot be searched as clear.
The Tibetan line has 'the towns of the land' for śāsana; its comment (m5) quotes this as yul gyi and glosses yul as the sense objects, in line with Munidatta's reading.
Here svarūpa is rang bzhin, the word the Tibetan also uses for svabhāva; in song 46 (m6) it is ngo bo.
Munidatta's lemma reads dāṭai, 'burns', where the verse (4a) has phāṭai, 'splits'; the Tibetan verse line also ends in tshig, 'burnt', so both read burning there.
Munidatta's viṭanāḍikā, mūtranāḍī and śukranāḍikā come out as dri chen gyi rtsa, dri chu'i rtsa and khu ba'i rtsa.
As in song 46, the vocative bho anadhigatamārga, 'you who have not reached the path', becomes kye'i lam ma rtogs pas, 'O, since you have not understood the path'.

questions: cp.47.h1 and cp.47.m7 are themselves Tibetan reading text, with no Bengali or Sanskrit behind them, so no equivalents are given for them.

vayu (পবন, cp.47.m5): not matched. The Tibetan has nothing for Munidatta's navaguṇam iti navapavanañ ca, 'the nine qualities are the nine winds'; it goes straight from lalanā and rasanā to yon tan dgu dang yul gyi, so there is no rlung to match.
upaya (োপায়, cp.47.m6): not matched. The Tibetan dpal gyi bla ma'i zhabs kyis, 'by the glorious guru's feet', renders śrīgurucaraṇa but has no thabs for -upāyena.
fire and smoke in the comments (m3, m4, m5) are given from the verse lines only; the comments use the same words (me, mes, du ba).
Witness flag, not a term (cp.47.m4): the Tibetan ye shes kyi me ni mi mthong, 'the fire of knowledge is not seen', supports Shastri's queried restoration [na?].

Witness flag, not a term (cp.47.3a): the Tibetan line opens rtswa ni 'bar ba ma yin, 'the grass does not burn', apparently taking khara as straw. The comment's lemma (m4) has rtsa, perhaps a scribal slip for rtswa.
Pada numbering, not a term: m5's tṛtīyapadena is rkang pa gnyis pas, 'by the second pada', in the Tibetan, which repeats m4's number.
